full_judgment: 2. Facts, in brief, are that the respondent No.1, as plaintiff, filed the above Mortgage Suit No.63 of 1994 praying for a preliminary decree for Tk.78,70,728/- as  on 31.10.94 with interest @ 20% per annum including penal interest and also praying that in case of the failure of the defendant petitioner to pay the decreetal dues, to make the decree final and direct sale of mortgaged properties and also to pass a personal decree against the defendant petitioner in respect of the shortfall amount after sale of mortgaged properties. The petitioner contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations and stating that the suit is not maintainable and barred by the principal of limitation estoppel, waiver and acquiescence. Thereafter while the suit was fixed for peremptory hearing, the defendant petitioner, filed an application terming the same as the "additional written statement" without mentioning therein any provision of the Code of Civil Procedure and made out a new case in the name Of additional written statement and prayed for accepting the said additional written statement. Though the learned advocate of the respondent No.1 received the copy with "objection" and by filing a petition also prayed for allowing him time to file written objection the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), by order dated 21.7.1999, accepted the said additional written statement without giving any opportunity to the respondent No.1 to file any written objection. The respondent No.1 then filed Writ Petition No. 2023 of 1998 challenging the above order dated 21.7.1997 and the High Court Division, after hearing, made the Rule absolute.
